scope: Renaming a safety tag that the safety program uses, through a single tag_set with safetyAcknowledged=true: scripts/qualify_safety_drive_tags.py --safety-tag-rename at b61ff94f, 35/35 steps (artifacts/sd/u3), and the same runner without the flag as regression guard, 21/21 steps (artifacts/sd/u4). Host and worker are the Debug build of 90d20b07, byte-identical to local.safety.tag-rename.20261111; the fixture helper is rebuilt with its new safety-bit-tag command. Fixture as in that record: an owned TIA V21 scratch with a CPU 1511F-1 PN 6ES7 511-1FL03-0AB0/V4.1 (configureScratchSecurity, failsafeRuntimeAccess; owned scratch only) as IO controller of a SINAMICS G120C PN with PROFIsafe telegram 30. The fixture helper created the Bool tag SafeDrive_Bit0 at %I0.0, bit 0 of the telegram's input, which read back with isSafety true. safety_import_xml then replaced the one empty F-FBD network of the generated main safety block Main_Safety_RTG1 with SafeUsed (%M10.2) := SafeDrive_Bit0 and applied with checkpoint, compile including the safety program (0 introduced errors) and save; the collective and software offline signatures changed with that import, as expected. The eight refused preparations of local.safety.tag-rename.20261111 were repeated on this tag and left every tag unchanged. The acknowledged rename of SafeDrive_Bit0 to SafeDrive_StoActive prepared with safetyTagRename, safetyBefore and the warning, and applied with checkpoint, baseline compile, safety_tag_rename_verified, compile (0 introduced errors) and save. The tag read back as SafeDrive_StoActive at %I0.0, Bool, isSafety true, and every other tag was unchanged. Main_Safety_RTG1 named the new tag and no longer the old one and was consistent. All four offline signatures (collective, software, hardware, communication address) and the F-runtime group were identical in safetyBefore and safetyAfter. change_restore of the rename returned the checkpoint.
limitations: One Bool safety tag on one bit of a PROFIsafe telegram 30, read by one F-FBD network of the generated main safety block on one owned F-CPU 1511F-1 PN. Other F-blocks, F-LAD, a tag used in several blocks or in an F-FB's interface, safety tags on F-I/O modules and tags in software units are not exercised.

The signatures were unchanged in this fixture. That is one observation on TIA V21, not a rule: compare safetyBefore and safetyAfter on every rename and treat a changed signature as a changed safety program.
The Bool safety tag was created by the qualification fixture, because tag_create refuses every address inside an F-I/O range; the PROFIsafe telegram was inserted by the fixture too.
The safety offline program had no password, so the SafetyLoginRequired refusal is covered by the shared guard of the other safety kinds only.
No safety acceptance, password or download. Engineering evidence only, not machine safety acceptance.
